I changed nothing and verified nothing. This session only has read and search tools, so I can't edit files or run commands, and the repo has no tests. What follows is a read-only audit with fixes I'm proposing, not fixes I applied.

**What I found:** Neither subsystem is over-engineered and neither has dead code, so keep both (the record calls this KEEP). There are 6 correctness defects. Your premise that the two share no files is wrong: `src/shipping/index.js:1` imports `load` from `src/orders/repository.js`, so they can't be split into independent parallel jobs.

**Why it matters:** A fix to the orders storage or the order data shape also changes shipping. Fixing them separately would break shipping without anyone noticing. Three of the defects depend on what the business wants (when tax applies, whether invoices can be changed, what "weight" means), and guessing would bake a wrong rule into billing.

**Do this first:**
1. Answer the three questions under "Defects" (D1, D2 and D5). The fix and the test for each depend on your answer.
2. Run this again in a session that has edit and shell tools, so I can fix D3 and D4, add `node --test` tests and run them.

**What I did not check:**
- Requirements grounding was not run. It is waiting on the three questions.
- A, L, C, E, H and Y were not run. The gate before them is blocked.
- `test-strategy` was not run. Nothing has been fixed yet, so there is nothing to test.
- Verification was not run. There are no test files, and `npm test` can't be run here.
- Edit history wasn't checked, because this isn't a git repo.

### Defects

| # | Where | Defect | Fix |
|---|---|---|---|
| D1 | `src/orders/index.js:6` vs `:14` | `placeOrder` stores the total without tax, but `reprice` stores it with tax. So `order.total` means different things depending on which function wrote it last. | **Question:** should `total` include tax? If yes, `placeOrder` needs a country. If no, `reprice` should store tax in its own field. |
| D2 | `src/orders/index.js:12-17` | `reprice` changes `total` but leaves `invoice` alone, so `invoice.total` no longer matches. | **Question:** can an invoice be changed after it's issued? If yes, rebuild it in `reprice`. If no, issue a credit note and a new invoice. |
| D3 | `src/orders/billing.js:16` | A country that isn't in the tax table, or is written in a different case, gets 0% tax without any error. | Throw an error for unknown countries, unless zero-rated countries are intended. If they are, list them explicitly. |
| D4 | `src/orders/index.js:13`, `src/shipping/index.js:4` | `load` of a missing ID gives `undefined`, which then crashes with an unclear `TypeError`. | Make `load` throw a clear "order not found" error. Shipping uses `load` too, so its behaviour changes as well. |
| D5 | `src/shipping/index.js:5` | `weight` is set to the number of order lines. It ignores quantities and has nothing to do with real weight. | **Question:** where should weight come from? Order lines have no weight data today. |
| D6 | `src/orders/billing.js:10-23` | Money is calculated with floating-point numbers. Invoice line amounts are before the discount and there is no discount line, so they don't add up to `total`. | Work in whole cents, and add a discount line to the invoice. |
